---
title: Authoring terms and acronyms
description: Define entries, choose reference forms, and control generated lists.
---

## Terms and acronyms are different

A glossary term names a concept, while an acronym records a short and long
form. Keep them distinct in the vocabulary:

```yaml
entries:
  - id: reproducible-research
    term: reproducible research
    definition: Research with documented data, methods, and computations.

  - id: doi
    kind: acronym
    short: DOI
    long: digital object identifier
    short-plural: DOIs
    long-plural: digital object identifiers
    definition: A persistent identifier for a digital object.
```

The first automatic reference to [[doi]] uses the long and short forms. A
later [[doi]] uses the abbreviation. Explicit forms let the author override
that state when the sentence requires it.

## Reference forms

| Markup | Rendered intent |
|---|---|
| `[[key]]` | Automatic singular form; expand an acronym on first use |
| `[[key\|plural]]` | Automatic plural form |
| `[[key\|short]]` | Acronym short form |
| `[[key\|long]]` | Acronym long form |
| `[[key\|full]]` | Acronym long and short forms |
| `[[key\|short-plural]]` | Explicit short plural |
| `[[key\|long-plural]]` | Explicit long plural |
| `[[key\|full-plural]]` | Explicit full plural |
| `[[key\|symbol]]` | Associated symbol |
| `[[key\|cap:plural]]` | Capitalized semantic form |
| `[[key\|custom wording]]` | Literal visible wording |
| `[[key\|=plural]]` | Literal word that would otherwise select a form |
: Supported authoring forms. {#tbl-reference-forms}

For example, [[sample-size|cap:plural]] may differ between studies. The
associated symbol is [[sample-size|symbol]].

References expand in the body and in the `title`, `subtitle`, `description`,
and `abstract` metadata. Code and other metadata stay literal.

Inside a pipe table, escape the pipe so the table keeps its columns: `[[key\|plural]]`.

## Rich definitions

Definitions may contain Markdown emphasis, links, mathematics, and Pandoc
citations. Use a shorter, plain-language `tooltip` when the complete
definition is too long for an HTML balloon:

```yaml
- id: sample-size
  term: sample size
  plural: sample sizes
  symbol: $n$
  definition: The number of units in an analysis, represented by $n$.
  tooltip: The number of units included in an analysis.
```

## Related terms

Use `see` for a preferred term and `see-also` for related concepts. Both
accept one key, a comma-separated value, or a YAML list. Unknown related keys
fail the render, preventing broken scholarly cross-references.

## Custom list labels and anchors

```markdown
::: {#terms .glossary
      title="Terminology"
      acronym-title="Abbreviations"
      acronym-id="abbreviations"
      level="2"}
:::
```

Set `include-unused: true` to print the complete vocabulary. The default is
`false`, which keeps lists specific to the rendered document.

## Headings and navigation

`## [[reproducible-research]]` becomes a plain heading. It counts as a use but
does not create a nested link, definition balloon, or first-use acronym side
effect. This keeps website sidebars and tables of contents aligned.
